notes.s: A boy performing tough-guy swagger while visibly having no idea what he is doing.
notes.t: Second single from Skool Luv Affair in February 2014, the one with the school hallway and the water. The Korean title is the joke the English title drops: 상남자 is early-2010s slang for a he-man who does everything head-on. What the verses actually show is a kid asking his father how he confessed to his mother, refreshing her profile photo and watching a read receipt vanish. The distance between the pose and the behaviour is the song, and Korean fans now talk openly about how badly the grab-me hook has aged.
k: The 상 is the 上 of upper or top grade, so 상남자 is a top-tier man, the sort who does not deal in hints. The word was internet slang of the period, half admiring and half mocking, and it is the boast the title makes before the verses undercut it. Boy In Luv keeps none of that.

오빠 is what a woman calls an older male she is close to, so asking to become her 오빠 is asking for a position, not a nickname. 되고파 is a compressed poetic 되고 싶어, and it exists mainly so that 고파 can land twice, first as want to become and then as hungry in the next line. That rhyme is the hook.
일 자리 없어, 짐과 동시에 속만 타지

KakaoTalk marks a sent message with the number of people who have not read it yet. In a one-to-one chat that number is 1, and the instant she opens the message the 1 disappears. So the line is: the 1 is gone, and the second it goes my insides burn. 속이 타다 is the idiom for exactly that burn, used for worry and impatience. This is 2014 messenger life, and nothing in the English hints at it.

-대다 bolts onto a sound or manner root and means to keep behaving that way. 틱틱 is snapping at someone, 씩씩 is huffing, 징징 is whining, and stacking three in a row is a tantrum rendered as a list. The -게 되다 on the end means he ends up like that rather than choosing it. Learn that pair and a large chunk of Korean mimetic vocabulary opens up.
